sentences.text: SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT KALABURAGI DATED 08.02.2018, IN MVC NO.561/2015.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.561/2015 vide its judgment and award dated 08.02.2018.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 09.01.2015, when he was hit by a moving car bearing registration No.KA-29/M-5178 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').
The claimant claimed that he suffered fracture of the left femur and other injuries and was treated as an inpatient, where after a surgery, his left leg was shortened by 3.5 cm.
He claimed that he was agricultural labourer and due to the shortening of the limb, he was left permanently disabled and therefore, was deprived of the ability to earn any NC: 2023:KHC-K:5508 income.
He claimed that he was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
Hence, he filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The insurer contested the claim petition and contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence and therefore, it was not liable to indemnify the owner.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P12.
He also examined one doctor as PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered fracture of left femur and that the left limb was shortened by 3.5 cm.
He also deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 25% to the whole body.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the tribunal held that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident that happened on 09.01.2015.

It noticed the medical evidence and held that the claimant had suffered fracture of femur of the left leg and post surgery, the claimant had Jagadevappa @ Jagadev vs Satishkiumar And Ors on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199432456/
2 suffered shortening of the left limb by almost 3.5 cm.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The NC: 2023:KHC-K:5508 Tribunal assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 8% and his notional income was considered at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and the following compensation was awarded:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 15,000/-
 2 Attendant charges, food and 15,000/-
 conveyance charges  3 Loss of future income 74,900/-
 4 Loss of income during treatment 6,000/-
 5 Loss of amenities and nutrition 10,000/-
 food  Total 1,20,900/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is in appeal.
7. The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant was 48 years old as on the date of the accident and was an agricultural labourer.

Shortening of the limb would NC:
2023:KHC-K:5508 leave the claimant perpetually limping, which would certainly affect his ability to be employed as an agricultural labourer.
He contended that the assessment of disability by the Tribunal was without any basis.

He submitted that since the disability was permanent, the Tribunal must have accepted the evidence of PW.2 who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 25% to the whole body.

He also submitted that the notional income of the claimant was considered at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month while in similar circumstances, it must have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
He also contended that the compensation awarded under other heads also deserve enhancement.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the disability suffered by the claimant as well as the notional income considered by the Tribunal and the compensation awarded under the other heads are just and proper and do not warrant any enhancement.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurer.
The claimant was an agricultural labourer and was aged 48 years at the time of the accident.

The medical evidence on record namely, Exs.P6, P9 and P10 indicate that the claimant had suffered fracture of left femur and that post surgery to fix the fracture, left limb of the claimant was Jagadevappa @ Jagadev vs Satishkiumar And Ors on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199432456/
3 shortened by 3.5 cm.

entities.text: Jagadevappa @ Jagadev vs Satishkiumar And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This would mean that the claimant would be limping forever and would definitely result in a permanent disability which would affect his ability to be employed as an agricultural labourer.

In that view of the matter, factoring functional disability caused due to the injury as well as physical disability, this Court considers it appropriate to assess the disability suffered by the claimant at 20% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimant, the notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
Taking into account the above, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-

Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2 Attendant charges, food and 15,000/-
 nourishment charges

3 Loss of income during the 24,000/-
 period of treatment for  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5508  three months  4 Loss of income due to 2,49,600/-
 disability

5 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 6 Future medical expenses 10,000/-
 Total 3,68,600/-
11.

Since the liability of the insurer is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
12. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.1,20,900/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,68,600/-, which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

13. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
